title: The overhead meter divides a GATE's wall by a test-only denominator
body:
## Summary

`print_run_overhead` divides the **gate's** wall by a denominator made only of **test suites**. Where a gate wraps non-test work, the ratio is exact arithmetic about the wrong subject.

`DEVBIN_RUN_T0` is set in `open_run_log` -- the one point every gate passes through -- so the wall is the gate's whole span. `fullcycle` is itself a gate (`run_gate --label fullcycle --suffix FULLCYC`), and its log tees all three phases, so the parser picks up the test phase's `finished in` lines while the wall covers clean and build as well.

Measured by `intent/dc` on hv's run, 2026-09-01:

    overhead: 4.87x -- 170s wall against 34.91s of reported test time across 14 suite(s).

170 / 34.91 = 4.87 exactly, and 34.91 is the true sum of the 14 values. **103 of those 170 seconds were never going to be tests** -- a cold release build and a clean. The test phase alone is 61s against 34.91s = **1.75x**, which on the meter's own published scale (1.14x quiet, 80x eating the machine) is a quiet apparatus.

**So the line read as a real finding on a machine that was fine.**

## Why this is a FOURTH limit and not an instance of the three

The function declares three limits, deliberately in the code. None covers this: a runner **was** reporting; the tests were **not** slowed; the binaries **did** run sequentially. The unstated assumption is that **the wall being measured is a test run** -- true of every verb that existed when the meter was written, and false the moment `fullcycle` wrapped other verbs around one.

## And the self-check cannot reach it, by construction

Limit 3 gives the meter a free self-check: sub-1 reports UNDEFINED, catching parallelism. **Parallelism pushes the ratio DOWN. Non-test work pushes it UP**, into the range that looks like a finding.

**So the meter's only alarm fires in the direction that means "my model broke" and is silent in the direction that means "your machine is loud".** That is the direction nobody audits.

## What has been done, and what has not

**Done (2026-09-01):** the fourth limit is stated in the code beside the other three, and the output line now names its numerator as the GATE's wall, with an explicit clause that the wall covers everything the gate ran, tests or not. Wording only -- no number changes.

**Not done:** whether such a gate should carry a per-phase T0, time only its test phase, or keep reporting a whole-cycle figure.

## The open question

`fullcycle` may well **want** a whole-cycle number: a cycle spending 60% of its wall on a cold release build is a true and useful fact. `intent/dc` explicitly did not prescribe, and neither does this issue. The defect was that one line said `reported test time` while its numerator was a cycle; the remaining choice is between the denominator, the label, and a per-phase T0.

## Provenance

`intent/dc` re-derived both terms off the log rather than trusting the printed line, and asked that the mechanism be verified in `runlog` before anyone acted on it -- their own caution after a measured-but-wrong mechanism cost an hour earlier the same day. Verified here: the mechanism is `run_gate` wrapping `fullcycle`, which they had as "T0 set at the top of the cycle". Same effect, and the conclusion stands unchanged.
